When printing official ballots you give each ballot a unique GUID and sign it with the official key of the Secretary of State. You print that as a Data Matrix code in several places on the ballot (in case on or two gets jacked up). When counting votes the tabulator scans the code and checks the GUID and makes sure the signature is valid. Each GUID can only count once. If more than one instance of a GUID is encountered, both ballots are set aside for investigation.
